proof_scope: the three peer target types /ask can address: Herdr sessions via monitor-herdr, model calls via tau, and web models via surf

claims.proves: each target type is addressable by name, that a Herdr name collision refuses to guess and surfaces session/model/directory for interview, that dead and busy panes are never typed into, and that compiling a model or web-model seat never goes provider-live without --execute; and that a message sent through `ask herdr send` actually appears in the live target pane, confirmed by an independent read; and that communication is bidirectional -- the target agent replies and the reply is captured; that a pane still redrawing is never sent to; that seat windows land on the reviewer desktop verified by wmctrl rather than by the mover; and that tab age on a cold ledger reports lower bounds rather than claiming exact ages; and that a provider whose probe timed out or failed is removed before dispatch with its real failure code, so the caller receives a terminal artifact instead of waiting (#1397); and that a compiled request carries the same goal_hash as its DAG, so the terminal join seam cannot fail after provider spend (#1399); and that ask.run_projection.v1 reports every compiled node including those that produced no artifacts at all, deterministically, across the real run corpus (#1401)
claims.does_not_prove: that a targeted agent understood or acted on a delivered message, browser or model semantic correctness, or that a Herdr session works as a roundtable seat (no capture lane exists yet)

cases.name: run-projection-survives-the-real-corpus
command:
cd .. && uv run python -c "import sys,collections; sys.path.insert(0,'src')
from pathlib import Path
from ask.run_projection import project_run
root=Path('/mnt/storage12tb/skills/ask/outputs/.ask_artifacts/tau-dag-runs')
dirs=sorted([d for d in root.iterdir() if d.is_dir()])[:300]
if not dirs: print('SKIP: no run corpus available'); raise SystemExit(0)
stages=collections.Counter()
for d in dirs:
    p=project_run(d)
    for n in p['nodes']: stages[n['stage']]+=1
assert stages, 'no nodes projected'
assert stages.get('COMPILED',0)>0, 'a corpus with no never-started nodes means absence is being dropped'
print('projected', len(dirs), 'real runs; stages', dict(stages))"
